Fun fact for today’s edit: a lot of people see tigers and automatically assume they aren’t that good at camouflage. Bright orange doesn’t blend in very well with vibrant greens of their tropical forest right? And definitely not well with the stark snowy white for some tigers. Well, that’s what we humans see, but for the eyes of a tigers prey, which are usually small hoofed mammals like antelope or wild boars, they have dichromatic eyes, meaning they cannot see red hues, which includes orange. So a bright orange tiger that people think to be very conspicuous and not sneaky at all, is almost invisible in a green jungle. Orange and red colors become green to the eyes of a tigers prey, allowing the tiger to easily sneak up undetected, and a tigers black stripes only benefit the camouflage even further. My favorite feature of a tiger is the cute white dots on the back of their ears, which act as a second pair of eyes, not meaning they can see out of those spots, but that they look like a pair of eyes which can deter predators from attacking because in the wild, when a predator is detected by its soon to be food, it usually leaves since the element of surprise isn’t in their favor. - #tiger #animals #edit #fyp #fypシ゚viral @lay ᢉ𐭩 @𓂃⟡ ݁꒰kyky ( ˶ˆᗜˆ˵ )꒱ ⸝⸝  .ᐟ . @danny🐟 @?🧩 @ana @🦌

The tiger (Panthera tigris) is the largest living cat species, recognised by its powerful body, sharp claws, muscular limbs, and distinctive orange coat covered in black stripes. Tigers are skilled hunters with exceptional night vision, strong jaws, and the ability to move quietly through dense vegetation. Unlike most cats, they are also excellent swimmers and often use rivers and lakes to cool down or travel. Tigers symbolise strength, courage, independence, and raw power. They inhabit forests, grasslands, mangroves, and other environments across parts of Asia. Unlike lions, tigers are generally solitary animals, patrolling large territories and hunting prey such as deer and wild boar. Despite their strength, they face serious threats from habitat loss, poaching, and conflicts with humans. Fun fact: Every tiger has a unique pattern of stripes, and the markings extend onto its skin beneath the fur. No two tigers have exactly the same stripe pattern.  #Tiger #PantheraTigris #Wildlife #BigCats #Nature

IB taken from moot: @/ princesspupppysparkles  Aka flurry aka py the goat. she has cool edit with this sound ok🥺❤️ ♯ The Sundarbans mangrove tiger is a uniquely adapted population of the Bengal tiger that rules the largest mangrove forest in the world, spanning the border of India and Bangladesh. To survive in this harsh, flooded environment, these tigers have evolved a smaller, leaner body weight (averaging 75 to 115 kg, compared to the 180 kg of mainland tigers) which prevents them from sinking into the soft mudflats. They are exceptional long-distance swimmers, capable of crossing fast-moving tidal channels up to 20 kilometers wide, and possess a highly muscular tail base that acts like a rudder in turbulent waters. Because constant tides wash away scent markings, they are highly nomadic and have adapted to a flexible diet that includes crabs, fish, monitor lizards, and water snakes, alongside traditional prey like spotted deer. Uniquely, they are also capable of drinking brackish water when fresh water is scarce. Today, this highly specialized population is strictly protected within the Sundarbans National Park and facing critical challenges from climate-induced rising sea levels.
